subject: Final-mile buffer allocation & contingency sync
messages:
From: Sophia Adams <s.adams@orangetech.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: OrangeTech Procurement <procurement@orangetech.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Delivery cadence and final mile — timeline impact

Ben —

Quick note from procurement: a supplier delay has pushed one dependent milestone ~10 business days. That cascades to our internal UAT window and threatens the planned go-live week of Jan 18. We need to understand how that shift would affect the MAP and any evaluation gates you folks require.

Can you outline the simplest contingency you can accept that preserves the current commercial terms (or note what concessions would be required)? We attached our latest evaluation schedule for context.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Sophia Adams
VP of Product
OrangeTech

Attachments: OrangeTech_MVP_Eval_Schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sophia Adams <s.adams@orangetech.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 11:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Delivery cadence and final mile — timeline impact

Hi Sophia —

Thanks for the heads up and the schedule — appreciate the details. Short answer: we can accommodate a ~10 business day slip but we recommend a small, structured buffer rather than a blanket date move so we keep momentum on evaluation artifacts that aren’t supplier-dependent. Two pragmatic options: 

Option A — Staged buffer (recommended)
- Add a 10-business-day buffer to supplier-dependent milestones only (integration + hardware validation).
- Keep the original UAT start date for software-only tests; move joint UAT kickoff if integration verification fails.
- No change to pricing or final SOW; billing milestones remain as-is unless integration scope materially expands.

Option B — Global re-baseline
- Move MAP milestones forward by 10 business days across the board.
- Requires an updated SOW amendment (DocuSign) and one-time schedule credit equivalent to 5% of the first-month invoice to cover the extended committed runway.

Operational asks from our side:
- Which supplier milestones are fixed vs flexible? (we only push dependent tasks)
- Confirm whether OrangeTech’s procurement needs any paperwork changes to preserve January capacity reservations.

I attached a short proposal (two pages) showing how staged buffers map to the existing MAP so you can share internally. If you want, we can lock Option A now and leave Option B as a fallback.

Preferred next steps: you confirm Option A/Option B, I’ll update the MAP and post an annotated timeline to HubSpot, then we route any necessary contract amendment to DocuSign.

—Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132

Attachments: BC-MapBufferProposal_v1.pdf (pdf)
Related: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/ORG-2319

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: risk entries for OrangeTech — supplier slip (for LA)

Ben / Laura —

I updated the close risk log with the supplier slip and recommended mitigations. Key entries below (abbrev):

- Risk ID: ORG-2319-R1
  - Description: Supplier delay -> 10 business day shift in integration milestone
  - Impact: UAT compression (high), potential invoice timing shift (medium)
  - Likelihood: Likely
  - Mitigation: Apply staged buffer; run parallel software-only UAT; escalate procurement hold if integration not signaled by 12/28
  - Owner: rishi_malhotra

- Risk ID: ORG-2319-R2
  - Description: Contract amendment needed if customer chooses full re-baseline
  - Impact: Legal review time + SOW amendment (low-med)
  - Mitigation: Prepare two DocuSign templates (Option A memo, Option B amendment) and pre-clear finance for 5% schedule credit
  - Owner: laura_bennett

I’ve attached the CSV export of the updated risk log for audit. If Laura wants to escalate to CS leadership for an SLA exception or schedule credit approval, flag it and I’ll route.

-Rishi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: close_risk_log_20261218.csv (csv)

Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 16:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Delivery cadence and final mile — timeline impact

Ben / team —

Thanks — Option A (staged buffer) looks good to us. We want to preserve the January billing milestone if possible; procurement will confirm whether any paperwork is needed to hold capacity — I copied them.

Two quick asks before we lock: 
- Can you add a 3-business-day contingency window to the UAT kickoff (soft buffer) so we have breathing room if the supplier delivers late but not by the full 10 days?
- Please send the Option A memo (one-paragraph) for our legal team so we can sign quickly via DocuSign.

If you send the memo today, procurement will try to confirm the capacity hold by EOD tomorrow. Once legal signs the memo I’ll route to our PM for schedule coordination.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Sophia Adams
VP of Product, OrangeTech
